content.text:
**Observations**

- Layer‑1 weights are essentially noise (|w| ≲ 0.035) only in image row 0, row 27, and in columns ≈0–3 and ≈24–27 of every row. Everything inside that frame carries structure, and the structure starts already at **image row 1** (inputs 32–52, |w| up to 0.28) and rows 2–3 (inputs ~60–80, ~88–110, |w| up to 0.55), and it persists down to rows 25–26 (inputs ~700–750, |w| up to 0.47). So the informative region is a tall rectangle: nearly the full height of the image but only the central ~20 columns.
- The weights are organised as long, smooth horizontal bands rather than localized stroke/edge detectors: within one image row, a given hidden unit usually keeps the same sign across 15–20 consecutive columns (e.g. unit 7 is uniformly strongly negative along rows 1–3 and again along rows 17–23; unit 14 is uniformly negative along rows 2–3 and rows 24–26; unit 5 is uniformly positive along rows 24–26; unit 2 and unit 10 are strongly negative across rows 1–3). Several units (3, 4, 10, 15, 8) have broad blobs centred around rows 10–20 with left/right sign flips, i.e. they contrast the left side, the centre and the right side of the object (typical of "two legs / central gap vs. filled silhouette" or "wide vs. narrow object").
- Hidden units therefore look like coarse silhouette templates: "does the object touch the top edge (shoulders/collars)", "does it fill the bottom rows (shoes, trousers, long dresses)", "is the middle filled or split", "is the object wide at the bottom". Biases b1 are mostly negative, so units are off unless a sizeable region is bright.
- Output layer: W2 is dense, with every hidden unit contributing ±0.5–1.0 to many classes; no class is read out by one or two units, and the columns do not show the kind of sparse, almost one‑hot structure one gets with easily separable classes. Classes are distinguished by combinations of bands (e.g. class 1 is driven positively by units 7, 8, 11, 12, 15 and negatively by 0, 2, 4, 6, 9 — a signature of a tall, narrow, top‑to‑bottom object). b2 is modest; classes 5 and 2 have the largest positive biases, class 8 the most negative.

**Reasoning**

- MNIST / EMNIST / KMNIST‑style handwritten characters are size‑normalised into a 20×20 box centred in the 28×28 frame; a network trained on them has essentially zero weights in rows 0–3 and 24–27 (and columns 0–3, 24–27), because those pixels are always black. Here rows 1–3 and 24–26 carry some of the largest weights in the whole matrix, so centred handwritten characters are ruled out. Also, digit/character networks develop thin, stroke‑like, locally varying weight patterns, not 20‑pixel‑wide uniform horizontal bands.
- The informative region (full height, central ~20 columns, hard black margins left and right) plus smooth filled‑silhouette templates is exactly the statistics of Fashion‑MNIST: garments and shoes are rendered as bright filled shapes on black, vertically filling the frame (shirts/coats touch the top, trousers/dresses run top to bottom, shoes sit in the lower half) with dark side margins.
- The dense, non‑sparse W2 fits a dataset where several classes are near‑duplicates in silhouette (T‑shirt / shirt / pullover / coat; sneaker / sandal / ankle boot) and must be separated by weighted combinations of band detectors — a 16‑unit MLP on Fashion‑MNIST typically reaches ~85% with exactly this kind of readout.
- 28×28 grayscale with 10 classes also excludes CIFAR‑like natural images (colour, 32×32) and medical/other sets with different class counts.

**Dataset:** Fashion‑MNIST (Zalando clothing images, 28×28 grayscale, 10 classes).

**Classes:** 0 T‑shirt/top, 1 Trouser, 2 Pullover, 3 Dress, 4 Coat, 5 Sandal, 6 Shirt, 7 Sneaker, 8 Bag, 9 Ankle boot.

**Confidence:** 75%
